subject: Game Theory
title: Art Auction Secrets
description: A fast breakdown of Art Auction Secrets for builders.

hook.text: In 2017, a da Vinci painting sold for $450 million at Christie's—the most expensive artwork ever.

buildup.text: Art auctions use the English format: open, ascending bids with dramatic pauses and audience gasps.

discovery.text: Auction houses earn commissions from both buyer and seller, sometimes totaling 25% of the sale price.

twist.text: Guarantees complicate things: houses promise a minimum to the seller, then bear the risk if bidding falls short.

climax.text: Chandelier bidding—fake bids off the wall—is legal and common to create early momentum.

punchline.text: Art auctions sell stories, not just art.

quiz.question: What is 'chandelier bidding'?
options: Fake early bids to build momentum
